title: Preterite or imperfect?
tagline: The scene and the action, verbs that change meaning, and how to tell a story.
goal: Choose between the preterite and the imperfect in any story, including closed periods, interruptions and verbs like saber, conocer and querer.

blocks.text: English uses one past («I lived») for both. Spanish splits it: the **imperfect** paints the scene, the **preterite** moves the story forward.

head: Imperfect: the scene
Preterite: the events
rows: One time or counted times: *ayer, una vez, tres veces*

blocks.text: If you can ask «and then what happened?» after the verb, it's preterite.
A long action with clear limits is still **preterite**. Length doesn't matter; the limits do.

items.tr: I lived in Lima for ten years.
When I was a student, I lived in Lima.

items.fr: No {sabía} que estaba casado. Lo {supe} ayer.
items.tr: I didn't know he was married. I found out yesterday.

items.fr: {Conocí} a Nicolás en una parada de autobús.
items.tr: I met Nicolás at a bus stop.

items.prompt: De niño, ___ al fútbol todos los días.
___ diez años en Lima y después me mudé.
Cuando era estudiante, ___ en un cuarto pequeño.

exercises.title: The meaning changes
exercises.instructions: Choose the form that matches the English hint.

items.prompt: No ___ que tenías hermanos. (I didn't know)
Después de tres intentos, ___ abrir la puerta. (I managed)
Le pedí ayuda, pero no ___. (he refused)

exercises.title: A story
exercises.instructions: Write the verb in the preterite or the imperfect.

checklist: I use the imperfect for the scene and the preterite for events.
I use the preterite for closed periods, even long ones.
I know sabía / supe, conocía / conocí, quería / quise.
I tell a story mixing both tenses.

challenge.title: How you met
challenge.text: Tell how you met someone important in eight sentences: start with the scene in the imperfect, then the events in the preterite, and end with how you felt: *Era el verano de 2019. Hacía mucho calor. Entré a una cafetería y…*
